title: JSON and APIs: Talking to Other Programs
concepts: JSON and Python types: object, array, string, number, true, false, null
request, response, status code and body

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked for price_of(data, name) from a saved supplier response, the AI wrote data["items"][name]["price"] and said it returns 1.2 for milk. In the sample, items is a list, so the code stops with TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not str. The AI's next version looped over the list but returned the price as text, '1.20', and Asha's exact-value tests failed. Adding float() made every case pass.

changes: The curriculum's 'how web APIs work' is taught with a diagram and an illustrative urllib.request fragment against a placeholder address. Every runnable example reads a saved sample response instead of the network, so outputs are the same on every run and the checker needs no internet access.
The requests package is named only as the next chapter's topic, because installing packages is taught in Chapter 24.
is None is introduced in Step 2 as the PEP 8 way to check for None, because JSON null becomes None and the AI section needs the check.

The trailing comma case for JSONDecodeError was left out, because its message changed in recent Python versions; the lesson uses single quotation marks and an empty body, whose messages are the same on every supported version.
Sample data files (scone.json, weather_sample.json, prices.json, prices_today.json) sit beside the examples; the checker runs every example on a fresh copy of its folder.
outstanding_issues: On a learner's computer, the error reports show the full path to the file instead of the short file name, and the JSONDecodeError report lists the json module's own files.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
